title: Reg-tests timeouts
body: My HAProxy reg-test runs started taking an extra 5-6 minutes because four tests regularly fail after about two seconds: reg-tests/http-rules/acl_cli_spaces.vtc, reg-tests/mcli/mcli_show_info.vtc, reg-tests/mcli/mcli_start_progs.vtc, and reg-tests/connection/http_reuse_always.vtc. They passed with 3.0-dev4-7151076 but fail with 3.0-dev8-e158b7e in our GitLab CI environment. The failures report bad exit statuses and, for the mcli tests, assertions in haproxy_wait(). The environment is Linux in CI with a fairly ordinary linux-glibc build configuration.

symptoms_visible: Four reg-tests that used to pass now fail after roughly two seconds, and the complete CI run spends an extra five to six minutes waiting.
The failed results include bad exit statuses and haproxy_wait() assertions.
N0.label: N0 recurring reg-test timeouts reported

symptoms_visible: The same four tests still fail in newer development builds in our Kubernetes-hosted GitLab CI.
The issue does not occur in my GitHub Actions runs.
N1.label: N1 CI-environment dependence established

symptoms_visible: The affected tests still time out in GitLab CI after I updated vtest with the master-worker sd_notify patch.
N2_x.label: N2_x updated-vtest aftermath

symptoms_visible: After fixing a separate file-descriptor-limit problem, the same timeout behavior remains.
Verbose runs wait about two seconds during shutdown and then show the process being terminated with signal 15 and status 143.
Later CI runs have six tests exhibiting the timeout.
N3.label: N3 shutdown behavior captured

symptoms_visible: The unmodified CI build still has the delayed test shutdowns.
With the updated diagnostic patch applied, the complete reg-test set passes.
N4.label: N4 signal-path experiment succeeds

symptoms_visible: The same reg-tests still time out when I rerun without the diagnostic HAProxy patch, even after trying a dedicated init process such as tini.
N4_x.label: N4_x init-wrapper aftermath

symptoms_visible: The test timeouts remain in GitLab CI without the HAProxy patch.
The GitLab runner's surrounding command chain includes a backgrounded wrapper even though I do not explicitly start make in the background.
N5.label: N5 backgrounded execution context identified

symptoms_visible: With the merged HAProxy fix, the reg-tests pass normally in my GitLab CI and the extra six to seven minutes of idle waiting are gone.
N_terminal.label: terminal CI timeouts resolved

question_patterns: Does this still happen on a current development build?
Can you rerun the affected tests against the latest development revision?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. It still happens at least through 03ca16f: the same four tests fail after about 2.2 seconds.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No, all of the affected tests pass on the latest development build and the delay has disappeared.
It persists on a slightly newer development revision with the same four failures.

question_patterns: Does the same build fail in any other CI environment?
Can you compare the result with GitHub Actions or a local run?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not happen in my GitHub Actions workflow. I only see it in the GitLab CI jobs running as pods in our Kubernetes cluster.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same tests fail identically in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, and local runs.

edges.comment: Reporter c1-c2: the failure persists on 03ca16f but does not reproduce in the reporter's GitHub Actions environment, narrowing the issue to the Kubernetes-hosted GitLab CI execution context.

solution.intent: Update vtest to the branch containing the pending master-worker sd_notify support, on the theory that an outdated vtest causes these failures.
solution.concrete_example: Build vtest from the haproxy-sd_notify branch and rerun the failing master-worker reg-tests.

edges.comment: Participant1 c11 suggested the pending vtest master-worker update. Reporter c12 had already incorporated that patch into the retained vtest dependency, but the CI timeouts remained.

question_patterns: Can you run one affected test verbosely and paste the shutdown portion of the log?
What exit status and signal appear after the timeout?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In my verbose log, vtest sends Kill(2), then nothing finishes for about two seconds. It follows with Kill(15), and the worker exits with code 143. The log also says the expected exit is signal 2, status 0x82.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The process exits immediately after Kill(2) with code 130, but the test still fails for an unrelated assertion.
The delay is 2.3 seconds rather than 2.1 seconds, followed by the same Kill(15) and status 143 output.

question_patterns: Are the same tests still affected in the latest exhaustive run?
Which tests currently exhibit the timeout?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The original four still fail, and two more now show the same timing: reg-tests/mcli/mcli_debug_dev.vtc and reg-tests/server/abnsz.vtc.

edges.comment: Reporter c3 and c10 supplied detailed logs after fixing a separate open-file-limit issue. Participants c13-c15 compared the reporter's raw signal/status output with successful local shutdowns; the causal interpretation remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you apply this diagnostic patch to a test build and rerun the complete reg-test set?
Please rerun the CI job with the revised diagnostic patch and report the raw result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The last job with the updated patch passes all the tests. Without the corrected version, I still saw the same failures.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The complete test set still has the same six timeouts with the diagnostic patch applied.
All tests pass with the patch, but the run is still slightly slower than my GitHub Actions run.

question_patterns: Can you capture the process hierarchy while the reg-tests are running?
Which process is PID 1, and where are make, vtest, and HAProxy in the process tree?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the pod, bash is PID 1. The process tree during the reg-tests shows make, vtest, and HAProxy further down the chain; none of those is PID 1. I've attached screenshots from the same cluster and from the running reg-tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: HAProxy itself is PID 1 and has no parent process inside the container.

edges.comment: Reporter c26 and c30-c31: a test-only HAProxy patch with the corrected exit behavior made all tests pass, while process screenshots disproved the idea that make, vtest, or HAProxy itself was PID 1. These were measurement runs, not the final fix.

solution.intent: Place a dedicated init and signal-forwarding process such as tini at PID 1 in the CI container.
solution.concrete_example: Rebuild the CI image with tini or an equivalent PID-1 binary that launches the job shell as a child, then rerun without the diagnostic HAProxy patch.

edges.comment: Participants c29 and c34 proposed an init-system explanation. Reporter c32-c33 rebuilt the image and retested without the diagnostic HAProxy patch; tini and similar wrappers did not remove the timeouts.

question_patterns: Can you inspect the full command ancestry above the test job and check whether any wrapper command ends with an ampersand?
Does the GitLab runner's generated shell script contain an '&' on a command above make?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I don't start make in the background myself, but the process highlighted above it is GitLab CI's own wrapper and it is launched with '&'. GitLab generates that surrounding scripting for cloning, caches, artifacts, and the job commands.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is no backgrounded process anywhere in the ancestry; every wrapper uses a foreground wait and exec chain.
A different GitLab-generated ancestor is backgrounded, but make and vtest are still invoked normally by my job script.

edges.comment: Participant3 c35-c37 reproduced the symptoms when vtest had any backgrounded ancestor and pointed out the '&' in the process hierarchy. Reporter c36 and c38 identified that ancestor as GitLab runner-generated scripting; only the reporter's own observation is used as the answer.

solution.intent: Fix HAProxy master-worker shutdown so worker and program processes terminate correctly when vtest sends SIGINT, including when the test process has a backgrounded shell ancestor, then ask the reporter to verify the merged fix in the affected CI.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the HAProxy master-worker signal-handling fix so SIGINT from vtest stops the workers promptly instead of leaving them until vtest's two-second fallback SIGTERM. After the change is merged, rerun the normal GitLab CI job without the diagnostic patch or tini workaround and confirm that the reg-tests complete normally.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers reproduced the behavior by placing vtest beneath a backgrounded shell ancestor. They inferred that background-job signal semantics prevented workers and launched programs without explicit SIGINT handling from terminating, while the HAProxy master did react because it had a handler. This explains the reporter's raw sequence: SIGINT, a two-second wait, fallback SIGTERM, and status 143.

edges.comment: Participants c35-c41 established the final diagnosis and merged the HAProxy-side master-worker signal fix. Reporter c42 tested the merged result in the original GitLab CI environment and confirmed that it eliminated the failures and six-to-seven-minute delay.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final root cause: GitLab runner execution had a backgrounded shell ancestor, and under those job-control semantics HAProxy worker or program processes did not terminate on vtest's SIGINT even though the master handled it, causing vtest to wait and then send SIGTERM.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the two-second gap between Kill(2) and Kill(15), exit status 143 instead of the expected SIGINT status, the successful diagnostic worker-exit patch, and the backgrounded GitLab wrapper.
Must recommend the HAProxy master-worker signal-handling fix that promptly stops workers when vtest sends SIGINT, rather than treating a vtest update or a PID-1 init wrapper as the resolution.
Must not settle on updating vtest's sd_notify support or adding tini: both were tried in the affected CI and the timeouts remained.

Must ask the reporter to rerun the ordinary GitLab CI job on a build containing the fix, without the diagnostic patch, and only declare resolution after the reporter confirms that the tests pass without the idle delay.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical CI and HAProxy contributor who can rebuild dependencies and container images, apply diagnostic patches, inspect process trees, and provide exhaustive vtest logs, while openly noting uncertainty about Unix signal and job-control behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, candid, and collaborative; shares raw CI links and logs, corrects earlier conclusions promptly, reasons through hypotheses aloud, and confirms fixes enthusiastically.
